chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of God, Exalted and Mighty: 'And if you disclose [your] charitable expenditures or conceal them, indeed it is [always] good for you' (2:271). He said: 'It is in addition to zakat, for indeed zakat is public, not secret.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between concealing zakat and concealing voluntary charity in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the general virtue of concealing voluntary charity (sadaqat) and the specific jurisprudential ruling for obligatory alms-tax (zakat). He clarifies that while hiding charity is praiseworthy for its own sake, the zakat due to the Imam is inherently public to ensure transparency and proper distribution, thereby resolving the apparent tension between the Quranic verse and the requirement of public accountability in Shia fiqh.
